sections.name: Ch 1 · Your Future in Health Care

items.q: According to the text, the health care industry is the largest what in the United States?
items.a: Service employer
items.ex: Health care provides more than 22 million jobs, making it the largest service employer in the U.S.
w: Health care provides services, not manufactured goods.
Most health care jobs are not government jobs.
Health care is a service industry, not retail.

alt.q: Which description of the U.S. health care industry does the text give?
alt.ex: It provides more than 22 million jobs.
w: Health care delivers services, not products.
Health care is growing faster than average.
Health care is a service industry.

alt.q: A classmate says health care is the biggest service employer in the country. Based on the text, the classmate is:
alt.ex: The text states it is the largest service employer in the United States.
w: Incorrect; it is the second largest
The text calls it the largest.
The text names health care as the largest service employer.
The text refers to the whole United States.

items.q: About how many jobs does the health care industry provide in the United States?
items.a: More than 22 million
items.ex: The text states health care provides more than 22 million jobs.
w: About 2 million is the number of new jobs projected from 2021 to 2031.
The total is much larger, more than 22 million.
The text gives more than 22 million.

alt.q: The health care industry employs roughly how many people in the U.S.?
alt.ex: More than 22 million jobs.
w: 1.9 million is the yearly projected job openings.
4.3 is the trillions of dollars spent, not jobs.
95 million is the projected number of people 65+ by 2060.

alt.q: Which number best describes total health care jobs in the U.S.?
alt.ex: Health care provides over 22 million jobs.
w: 924,000 is the increase for home health and personal care aides.
The total is more than 22 million.
13% is the projected growth rate, not millions of jobs.

items.q: What does the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics project for health care employment from 2021 to 2031?
items.a: Growth of 13%, about 2 million new jobs
items.ex: BLS projects 13% growth and about 2 million new jobs, faster than the average for all occupations.
w: 2.7% is how much health care spending rose in 2021.
Growth of 46%, about 10 million new jobs
46% is the growth for nurse practitioners only.
A decline of 6%, losing 1 million jobs
Health care jobs are projected to grow, not decline.

alt.q: How fast is the health care industry projected to grow between 2021 and 2031?
alt.ex: This is faster than the average for all occupations.
w: 25% is the rate for home health aides, not the industry.
6% is the projected rate for registered nurses.

alt.q: Compared with the average for all occupations, the projected 13% health care growth from 2021 to 2031 is:
alt.ex: About 2 million new jobs are expected, faster than the average for all occupations.
w: The text says it is faster than average.
The text says it is faster than average.

items.q: Approximately [[1.9 million|1.9|1,900,000]] health care job openings are projected each year from growth and from replacing workers who left their jobs permanently.
items.ex: About 1.9 million openings are projected each year.

alt.q: Each year, about [[1.9 million|1.9|1,900,000]] health care job openings are expected because of growth and replacement of workers.
alt.ex: About 1.9 million openings are projected each year.

alt.q: Growth plus the replacement of workers who leave permanently creates about [[1.9 million|1.9|1,900,000]] health care openings per year.
alt.ex: About 1.9 million openings are projected each year.

items.q: In 2021, how much was spent on health care in the United States?
items.a: $4.3 trillion, about $12,914 per person
items.ex: Federal economists reported $4.3 trillion, an average of $12,914 per person, after a 2.7% increase.
w: 2.7% was the increase in spending, not the total.
$12,914 is the per-person amount, not trillions.
1.9 million is the yearly job openings figure.

alt.q: What was the average amount spent on health care per person in the U.S. in 2021?
alt.ex: Total spending was $4.3 trillion, or $12,914 per person.
w: 22 million is the number of jobs.

alt.q: By how much did U.S. health care spending increase in 2021?
alt.ex: Spending rose 2.7%, to $4.3 trillion.
w: 13% is the projected job growth for 2021–2031.
16% is the projected growth for medical assistants.
$4.3 trillion was the total spent, not the increase.

items.q: Match each occupation with its projected employment increase for 2021–2031 (Table 1–1).
items.ex: Nurse practitioners have the highest projected percentage growth in Table 1–1.

alt.q: Match each projected growth rate with the occupation it belongs to.

alt.q: Pair each health care job with its projected 2021–2031 growth percentage.
alt.ex: Nurse practitioners have the highest projected percentage growth in Table 1–1.

items.q: Which occupation in Table 1–1 has the highest projected percentage increase in employment from 2021 to 2031?
items.a: Nurse practitioners (46%)
items.ex: Nurse practitioners are projected to grow 46%, the highest in the table.
w: Home health aides grow 25%, less than NPs.

alt.q: A 46% projected growth rate belongs to which health care job?
alt.ex: NPs top Table 1–1 at 46%.

alt.q: Which job is growing fastest by percentage, according to the BLS data in the text?
alt.ex: Projected growth is 46% from 2021 to 2031.

items.q: Which occupation has the largest numerical increase in positions from 2021 to 2031 (Table 1–2)?
items.a: Home health and personal care aides
items.ex: Home health and personal care aides are projected to add 924,000 positions.
w: RNs add 195,400, second in the table.

alt.q: About 924,000 new positions are projected for which occupation?
alt.a: Home health and personal care aides
alt.ex: They have the largest numerical increase.

alt.q: Which job will add the most new positions (not the highest percentage) between 2021 and 2031?
alt.a: Home health and personal care aides
alt.ex: 924,000 new positions, far more than any other.
w: NPs have the highest percentage, but fewer positions.
PAs are not in the top numerical list.

items.q: Put these occupations in order from the LARGEST to the smallest numerical increase in positions, 2021–2031 (Table 1–2).
items: Home health and personal care aides (924,000)
items.ex: Home health aides add the most; nurse practitioners add the fewest of these four.

alt.q: Rank these jobs by how many new positions they will add, most first.
items: Home health and personal care aides (924,000)
alt.ex: Home health aides add the most; nurse practitioners add the fewest of these four.

alt.q: Put these occupations in order from the SMALLEST to the largest numerical increase in positions.
items: Home health and personal care aides (924,000)
alt.ex: Home health aides add the most; nurse practitioners add the fewest of these four.

items.q: Which of these are demands of health care work described in the text? Select all that apply.
o: Depending on the job, long hours are common.
It can involve dealing with the death of patients
This is one of the stresses named in the text.
It can require working quickly under pressure
The text lists this as a source of stress.
Routine assignments can be done automatically
Nothing can be done automatically, not even routine tasks.
Mistakes can be devastating, such as a wrong medication.
items.ex: Health care work is satisfying but demanding and must be taken seriously.

alt.q: A student asks what makes health care work stressful. Which answers match the text? Select all that apply.
o: Named as a demand of the work.
Named as a demand of the work.
Named as a demand of the work.
Never having to pay full attention
Full attention is required for everything.
alt.ex: Health care work is satisfying but demanding and must be taken seriously.

alt.q: Select every statement about health care work that agrees with the text.
o: Potential problems must be addressed before they become critical
The text says to note problems early.
All tasks must be done thoughtfully and conscientiously
Routine tasks can be done without thinking
Nothing can be taken for granted.

items.a: False

items.ww: All tasks must be performed thoughtfully and conscientiously.

alt.ex: Even routine assignments need thought and full attention.
alt.ww: The text says nothing can be done automatically.

items.q: Different sources agree on exactly which health care occupations have the fastest growth.
items.a: False
items.ex: The text notes that various sources give different occupations as fastest growing; its data come from BLS.
items.ww: Sources differ, which is why the text names BLS as its source.

alt.q: The text uses the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics as its source for job growth data.
alt.ex: The tables and projections come from BLS.
alt.ww: The growth figures are credited to BLS.

alt.q: Every source lists the same fastest-growing health care jobs.
alt.ex: Various sources give different occupations.

items.q: In 2019 there were [[52 million|52]] persons aged 65 and over, about 16% of the population.
items.ex: By 2060 this is projected to grow to 95 million people, or 23% of the population.

alt.q: About 16% of the U.S. population in 2019, or [[52 million|52]] people, were 65 or older.
alt.ex: By 2060 this is projected to grow to 95 million people, or 23% of the population.

alt.q: By 2060, people aged 65 and over are projected to number [[95 million|95]], or [[23%|23|23 percent]] of the population.
alt.ex: By 2060 this is projected to grow to 95 million people, or 23% of the population.

items.q: Why does the growing number of people aged 65 and over matter to health care?
items.a: It will drive the need for more health care professionals
items.ex: The 65+ population is projected to grow from 52 million (2019) to 95 million (2060).
w: It will reduce the number of health care jobs available
An older population needs more care, not less.
It will lower the demand for home health and personal care aides
Home health aides are among the fastest growing jobs.
It will make professional certification less important
Aging does not change certification rules.

alt.q: The text says the aging U.S. population will have what effect on health care?
alt.ex: Older adults use more health care services.
w: Demand grows as the population ages.
The text predicts growth in health care.
Many occupations will grow, such as home health aides.

alt.q: Which is a major implication of the 65+ population reaching 23% by 2060?
alt.a: Greater need for health care workers
alt.ex: This increase drives the need for more professionals.
w: More older adults means more care, not less spending.
Less demand for personal care and home health aides
Personal care aides are among the fastest growing jobs.
No change in health care jobs
The text calls the implications major.

Be honest and accept responsibility for your actions

Keep skills up to date and seek new knowledge

w: Teamwork is about cooperating with others.

w: Flexibility is about adapting to change.

alt.q: Keeping up with advances in technology and changes in how health care is delivered is part of being:

alt.q: A nurse calmly adapts when an emergency changes the day's plan. Which quality is shown?

items.q: According to the text, which is one of the most important qualities of a health care professional?

alt.q: Applying knowledge to decrease suffering and increase well-being describes which quality?

alt.q: Helping all patients regardless of race, religion, age, or lifestyle is part of which core quality?
